newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda says studying stake in Peugeot China venture.
newsitem.headline: Honda says studying stake in Peugeot China venture.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd said on Wednesday it is studying whether to take a stake in the Sino-French Guangzhou Peugeot Automobile joint venture.

Honda's auto parts venture in Huizhou, southern China, started making engine and suspension parts in November 1995 for export to Honda facilities elsewhere in Asia, but Honda has no car production unit in China.
"We are studying whether a purchase of a stake in China Peugeot would benefit us (Honda and its Chinese partner Dongfeng Automotive Group)," a Honda spokesman told Reuters.
"But there is no change in our policy. We plan to carry out our Chinese business with Dongfeng," the spokesman said.
In March, a spokesman for the PSA Peugeot Citroen group said the company had made no decision on whether to quit the joint venture, in which it owns 30 percent.
French newspapers have reported that the venture has been criticised by Chinese authorities for turning out dated models.
Honda is likely to cooperate on acquiring a stake in Peugeot's plant in Guangzhou if Dongfeng wants to take Peugeot's place, the spokesman said.
But a decision on selling Peugeot's stake is up to the Chinese government which has not disclosed what it wants to do, he added.

In March, the China Daily Business Weekly said South Korean automaker Hyundai Motor Co had applied to Chinese authorities for a 22 percent stake in the Sino-French Guangzhou Peugeot Automobile joint venture.
Media reports previously said General Motors, Ford and BMW were lined up to take Peugeot's place in Guangzhou if the French carmaker abandoned the project.
